title: Forensic Harvest Playbook — Customer Network Onboarding (PRD draft)
content:
Purpose and summary:
This draft outlines a lightweight but defensible forensic evidence collection and packaging playbook for customer-managed network onboarding in Private deployments. The goal is to give operators and customers a repeatable set of steps and APIs to collect actionable audit artifacts when onboarding or validating connectivity, configuration, and security posture — without shipping full packet captures or exposing sensitive customer payloads.

Problem statement:
- Customers and operator teams need a way to prove that acceptance checks, approval gates, and attestation steps actually ran and what they saw.
- Current ad-hoc artifacts (screenshots, hand-curated logs) are inconsistent and hard to verify during audits or incidents.
- We need a minimal, standardized evidence envelope that: preserves provenance, is tamper-evident, minimizes PII exposure, and is easy to consume by SRE/PS/Compliance.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: evidence collection during onboarding flow (connectivity test, firewall rules check, routing verification, TLS handshake proof, configuration diffs), artifact packaging, signatures, short-term retention, and operator UX for review.
- Out-of-scope: full packet capture ingestion, continuous full-fidelity network telemetry, forensic deep-dive tooling (separate project).

Success criteria (measurable):
- Onboarding playbook reduces time to sign-off by 40% in pilot customers.
- Evidence envelope contains at least: connectivity-snapshot, config-hash, service-cert-fingerprint, operator-verification-log, and an attestation signature.
- Evidence packages verified by two independent consumers (SRE and compliance) in pilot.

High-level design:
- Evidence types (minimal canonical set):
  - connectivity-snapshot: results of end-to-end TCP/TLS handshakes to endpoints, including latency and error codes (no payload).
  - config-diff: canonicalized customer network config (ACLs, routing tables) with redaction rules applied.
  - cert-fingerprint: leaf and intermediary cert fingerprints observed during TLS negotiation.
  - keystore-hash: optional HSM/KMS reference (not raw keys) if provided for signing.
  - operator-log: chronological operator actions and API responses (annotated).
  - sampling-probe: small pcap-lite (headers only, sampled) gated by customer consent and opt-in; default OFF.

- Evidence envelope format:
  - JSON manifest (schema v1) that lists artifacts, checksums, timestamps, source id, and operator id.
  - Each artifact is an opaque file with SHA256 checksum recorded in manifest.
  - Envelope signed with operator key and optionally customer verification key.
  - Tamper-evidence: manifest includes merkle-root over artifact checksums.

APIs and UX:
- Onboarding flow extension endpoints (examples):
  - POST /v1/onboard/{tenant}/collect?mode=minimal -> kicks off the canonical checks, returns collection-id.
  - GET /v1/onboard/{tenant}/collect/{id}/manifest -> returns signed manifest JSON.
  - GET /v1/onboard/{tenant}/collect/{id}/artifact/{name} -> fetch artifact (auth required).
  - POST /v1/onboard/{tenant}/collect/{id}/attest -> operator marks evidence as reviewed and publishes attestation.

Operator console changes:
- New "Evidence" tab in onboarding flows showing: status, artifacts list, redaction summary, signatures, and quick-download links.
- Inline checkboxes to grant or deny minimal sampling probe for this tenant (consent recorded as artifact).

Privacy and redaction policy:
- Default: redact IPs from application-level logs unless absolutely necessary; keep network metadata (src/dst subnet) hashed and salted per-tenant.
- Configuration diffs must be canonicalized and passed through redaction rules; sensitive fields (shared secrets, tokens) must be replaced with stable placeholders and hash references.
- Sampling probe only with explicit customer opt-in; sampling window and scope shown in UI and recorded in manifest.

Retention and export:
- Evidence packages retained for 30 days by default; export to customer S3 or GCS allowed with signed transfer token.
- Long-term archival only by explicit enterprise contract (e.g., 1 year).

Verification and tooling:
- Provide a small verification CLI (python) that accepts manifest + artifacts + public key and performs checks (hash, signature, merkle root).
- Provide simple Confluence playbook for auditors to validate packages manually.

Approval gates integration (how evidence gates map to approval steps):
- Gate: "Connectivity Verified" -> requires connectivity-snapshot artifact + operator attestation.
- Gate: "Firewall Rules OK" -> requires config-diff artifact + automated rule-checker results.
- Gate: "Certificate Verified" -> requires cert-fingerprint artifact and TLS handshake metadata.
- Gate: System will not transition to "Approved" unless required artifacts present and signatures verified.

Incident runbook (on evidence-related disputes):
1) Operator requests re-collection with increased sampling (customer consent required).
2) Compare previous manifest checksums; present diffs in UI.
3) If tampering suspected, escalate to security with full audit log export.

Operational considerations and performance:
- Collection jobs are rate-limited per-tenant; default quota tuned for onboarding bursts.
- Artifact storage uses inexpensive object store tier with lifecycle policies for auto-delete after retention window.
- Proof signing uses per-region operator signing keys rotated quarterly.

Open questions and risks:
- Customer acceptance: will customers permit any sampling even if limited? Proposed mitigation: default OFF and explicit consent with clear UI.
- Legal/regulatory: cross-border evidence retention implications for EU customers — need legal sign-off on export defaults.
- Verification scale: how many concurrent verification requests can the CLI/server handle? Need perf tests.

Next steps and plan (90-day roadmap):
- 0–2 weeks: align with Legal and Privacy on redaction rules and retention windows (owner: Priya).
- 2–6 weeks: prototype collection service and manifest schema; implement minimal connectivity-snapshot and cert-fingerprint collectors (owner: Eng-Infra + Applied-ML consult).
- 6–10 weeks: build UI evidence tab, attestation flow, and CLI verifier; run internal trial with Solutions Eng.
- 10–12 weeks: pilot with 2 customers; measure time to approval and gather feedback, iterate on redaction UX.

Appendix: example manifest (illustrative)
{
  "manifest_version": "v1",
  "collection_id": "col-20251104-az4f",
  "tenant": "acct-xyz",
  "artifacts": ["connectivity-snapshot.json", "config-diff.json", "cert-fingerprint.json"],
  "merkle_root": "<hex>",
  "signed_by": "operator-Asha",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-04T18:32:10Z"
}

Notes for reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: aim for minimal required artifacts that satisfy auditors while minimizing data sensitivity.
- Feedback specifically requested on: redaction rules (IP hashing vs partial redaction), consent UX for sampling probes, and signature model (operator-only vs dual-sign).

Contact: Priya Iyer (priya@redwood.ai) — add comments inline or ping #private-onboarding on Slack for quick sync.
